device_identification.what: Symmetric sidewall Bragg grating (rectangular-corrugated strip waveguide)
device_identification.how_it_works: A single-mode strip waveguide whose width is periodically modulated as a square wave. The periodic effective-index modulation creates a distributed Bragg reflector: light near the Bragg wavelength lambda_B = 2*n_eff*Lambda is reflected. Used as an in-line wavelength-selective mirror / filter. Corrugation is symmetric about the waveguide axis (both sidewalls pull in/out together), so the mode stays centered and the grating is TE-polarized-index modulation, not a mode converter.

evidence_from_image.symmetry: both top and bottom edges oscillate by ~12-13 px (edge pulls in symmetrically) -> symmetric width modulation about centerline

function_knobs.period_um: Bragg period Lambda -> sets Bragg wavelength lambda_B = 2 n_eff Lambda (THE defining knob)
function_knobs.w0_um: nominal (mean) waveguide width -> n_eff, single-mode operation
function_knobs.corrugation_um: full width swing dw = w_wide - w_narrow -> coupling coefficient kappa / bandwidth
function_knobs.duty_cycle: fraction of period at wide width -> harmonic content / apodization

iterations.change_made: Initial parametric Bragg grating: alternating centered rectangles, WIDE-first per period, w0=0.5, corrugation=0.099, period=0.319, 20 periods, duty=0.5125. Interior perfect; diff showed red/blue alternation at both corrugation bands = half-tooth horizontal phase offset.
Flipped per-period segment order to NARROW-first (target grating begins with a narrow segment, measured from pixel edge transitions). Phase aligned; only sub-pixel corner residuals remain.

knob_verification.note: homi.spec_optimization.verify_knob_response is MZI-specific (requires lengths.json with exactly 2 arms + delta_length_um); a Bragg grating has no interferometer arms, so a 2-arm lengths.json would fabricate structure the device lacks. Verified the most important function knob (period_um) instead with a direct gdstk geometry measurement (see knob_response.json).
